chunks: He was asked about the beggar who asks and it is not known what he is. He said: Give to the one for whom mercy occurs in your heart. And he said: Give less than one Dirham. I said: What is the most one can give? He said: Four Dawaneeqs.

key_terms.الدِّرْهَم: Dirham; a silver coin used as currency in early Islamic civilization
key_terms.الرَّحْمَة: mercy/compassion; the instinctive feeling of sympathy that moves one to give
key_terms.السَّائِل: beggar/one who asks; in Islamic jurisprudence, a person who solicits charity
key_terms.دَوَانِيق: Dawaneeqs (plural of Daniq); each Daniq is one-sixth of a Dirham, so four Dawaneeqs equal two-thirds of a Dirham

ai.seo_question: How much charity should a Muslim give to an unknown beggar according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides practical guidance on giving charity to unidentified beggars, instructing that one should follow the natural feeling of compassion in one's heart as a guide for whom to give. He sets a practical limit of less than one Dirham for such anonymous charity, with the maximum being four Dawaneeqs (roughly two-thirds of a Dirham), reflecting the early Islamic approach of encouraging generosity while setting reasonable parameters for distribution to unknown recipients.
word_analysis: Dawaneeqs (small coins, one-sixth of a Dirham each)
